$comment: Release notes for commits merged before they could declare their own with 'Release-note:' trailers. Read by build/scripts/SetReleaseNotesArgument.ps1. Each key is a full commit id; 'subject' is the commit's subject, checked to catch a wrong id; 'notes' replaces every note the commit would otherwise produce, and an empty list leaves it out. A note may have 'packages', the package IDs it is published for; without it, the note is published for every package the commit reaches. Categories: added, new, fixed, changed, deprecated, removed, breaking, none.

notes.text: When two observances of a calendar's VTIMEZONE begin at the same instant, GetUtcOffset now uses the last of them, as GetTransitions does, so ToUtc and ToLocal agree with the transitions

db8b5808bba187a1a01c679b0ef35f82c96bd71e.subject: Cache VTIMEZONE observance onsets by year (#263, #280) (#281)

notes.text: A VTIMEZONE RDATE onset no longer takes effect up to a second early for an instant with a fraction of a second
Resolving times through a calendar's own VTIMEZONE, the default resolver, is faster and allocates less, because observance onsets are now expanded once per year and reused

notes.text: Setting IcalAlarm.TriggerDateTime, or TriggerDuration on an alarm with an absolute trigger, now keeps the TRIGGER's other parameters and its position instead of dropping them and moving it to the end

56c0aeeb803c8e4ee8ceed4d1689405a5b675c91.subject: IcalTimeZoneResolver.Calendar rules give the right offset before a VTIMEZONE's first onset (#294)

notes.text: IcalTimeZoneResolver.Calendar rules give the right offset before a VTIMEZONE's first onset

319bcf011b3ae8b27eec7bc560c72bcd08359eb8.subject: Language tags that repeat a variant subtag or extension singleton are rejected (#318)

notes.text: A language tag that repeats a variant subtag or an extension singleton, ignoring case, is rejected as RFC 5646 requires, by `Create`, `TryCreate`, `IsWellFormedLanguageTagString` and the builder's `UsingVariantSubtags` and `UsingExtensionSubtags`

8c69c57005bf9342550d31c56bb1c694e10acdd7.subject: Default rules follow the RFC 5646 primary language subtag grammar (#320)

notes.text: Without a subtag registry, primary language subtags follow RFC 5646: one of five to eight characters must be letters only, so `12345` is rejected, and an extended language subtag must follow one of two or three letters, so `abcde-yue` is rejected
Without a subtag registry, four-letter primary language subtags, which RFC 5646 reserves for future use, are accepted as well-formed

fb24de6b9156b8db2f12f081b236c882a4c6ca5e.subject: Builder takes a UN M49 area through UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49Area) (#326)

notes.text: `Bcp47LanguageTagBuilder.UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49Area)` sets a UN M.49 area such as `UnM49Area._419` (Latin America and the Caribbean) as the region, and throws `ArgumentException` for a country

The builder's `UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49AreaByAlpha2CountryCode)` and `UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49AreaByAlpha3CountryCode)` overloads are obsolete, because they reject every member of those enums, and will be removed in v2.0; use `UsingRegionSubtag(UnM49Area)` or `UsingRegionSubtag(Iso3166Part1Alpha2Country)`

983790fa282c26c630e5065be0b2132a438952bd.subject: Language tag and subtag matching no longer depends on the current culture or accepts non-ASCII letters (#335)

notes.text: Language tag and subtag validation no longer depends on the current culture or accepts non-ASCII letters, so `IT` is accepted under the Turkish culture and the Kelvin sign (U+212A) is not accepted in place of `K`

eae2dbcc625c731b0291f3d03edd478a8a7d442d.subject: Default rules validate language tags with a parser instead of regular expressions (#322)

notes.text: Validation by the default BCP 47 rules uses a parser instead of regular expressions: the first Create is about 20 times faster, later calls 30 to 300 times faster, and validation no longer allocates
The netstandard2.0 build depends on System.Memory

fa92dfa9c0423fc27e102b6a675c20dfb30cbad5.subject: Language tags are checked against a Subtag Registry with a parser instead of regular expressions (#338)

notes.text: Checking a language tag against a Subtag Registry uses a parser instead of regular expressions: Create is about 10,000 times faster, the first call in a process takes milliseconds instead of more than a second, and checking no longer allocates
Creating language tags against the same Subtag Registry from several threads at once no longer throws or corrupts a shared cache
A Subtag Registry with no grandfathered records, or no records of some subtag type, no longer accepts the empty string or a tag with an empty subtag such as "en-"

7e8c6ce9762adc90656f31fb2d08f6ed44547947.subject: Default rules accept the grandfathered language tags as whole tags (#319)

notes.text: Without a subtag registry, the irregular grandfathered tags, such as `i-klingon` and `en-GB-oed`, are accepted as RFC 5646 requires

Without a subtag registry, regular grandfathered tags such as `art-lojban` are treated as whole tags, as they are with one: `PrimaryLanguageSubtag` is empty and the other subtag properties are `null` or empty

736c5c2458bf8e57f6f365f557b0e415c77b8835.subject: Default rules reject the unregistered region subtag 830 (#321)

notes.text: Without a subtag registry, the region subtag `830` (Channel Islands), which isn't in the IANA Language Subtag Registry, is rejected as RFC 5646 requires

efc410ebc3bb5a0dc7928b3b587ad52887c97267.subject: TryCreate(tag, registry, timeout, out) accepts tags that are valid only in the Subtag Registry (#333)

notes.text: `TryCreate(string, SubtagRegistry, TimeSpan, out Bcp47LanguageTag)` accepts tags that are valid only in the Subtag Registry, as the other registry overloads do

cf1066d2a70498b186c78e9b8f78893b688dc015.subject: Loading a Subtag Registry is about 2.3 times faster and allocates 73% less (#345)

notes.text: Loading a Subtag Registry is about 2.3 times faster and allocates 73% less

Loading a Subtag Registry unfolds a folded Description or Comments value with one space, skips an empty record or one with no File-Date, Subtag or Tag field instead of stopping there, and reads a field it doesn't know as a field of its own instead of appending it to the field before

496343f8601596f462338194deb06a6999fd014d.subject: Bcp47LanguageTag validates and parses spans of characters, and implements ISpanParsable and ISpanFormattable (#347)

notes.text: On netstandard2.0 and .NET 8 and later, `Bcp47LanguageTag.TryCreate`, `IsWellFormedLanguageTagString` and the `Check*` methods accept a `ReadOnlySpan<char>`; only `TryCreate` allocates, and only to copy a valid tag to a string. `AsSpan()` returns the tag without copying it
`Bcp47LanguageTag` implements `IParsable<T>` and `ISpanParsable<T>` on .NET 7 and later, and `ISpanFormattable` on .NET 6 and later

The new span overloads make a literal `null` or `default` argument to `TryCreate`, `IsWellFormedLanguageTagString` or a `Check*` method ambiguous on C# 7.3; cast it to `string`. On C# 10 and later, `IsWellFormedLanguageTagString` and the `Check*` methods can no longer be assigned to `var`; give the variable a delegate type such as `Func<string, bool>`. `Type.GetMethod(name)` throws `AmbiguousMatchException` for them; pass the parameter types. Compiled code is unaffected

11c7e3783e507ee0dc0da8bac146e3b092dcb0d9.subject: Decode and encode RFC 2231 parameter continuations, character sets and languages in MimeMediaType (#464)

notes.text: `MimeMediaType` decodes RFC 2231 parameter sections and extended values (character set and language), and rejects anything RFC 2231 doesn't allow unless the caller opts in with a `MimeMediaTypeParseOptions` member: `AllowMissingSections`, `AllowDuplicateSections` and `AllowLeadingZeroSectionNumbers` (together, `AllowNonstandardSections`), `AllowQuotedExtendedValues` and `AllowLowercaseHexDigits` (together, `AllowNonstandardExtendedValues`), `AllowUnknownCharsets` and `AllowInvalidOctets`
`MimeParameter` takes values that aren't US-ASCII and an optional RFC 1766 language, writes them as RFC 2231 extended values, and splits long parameters into sections with `FormatSections`

cae39430164072ed14e51c56eb318c32d30c0f71.subject: Readers and writers check the bytes of a body several times faster (#587)

notes.text: Read and write the vCard 4.0 extensions of RFC 6473, RFC 6474, RFC 6715, RFC 6869 and RFC 8605, with typed members on `VcardCard` and `IVcard40Card`

096696a5f4bf3dbbe407e90e2d535b134fbca422.subject: Read and write vCard 3.0 cards, and convert cards between versions (#620)

notes.text: Read and write vCard 3.0 cards (RFC 2426, RFC 2739 and RFC 4770) with `VcardReader` and `VcardOptions.WriteVersion`, and view them through `IVcard30Card`

`VcardCard` has `Mailer`, `Classification`, `SourceName`, `Profile`, `CalendarAccessUris` and `Agents` for the properties of older versions
Read and write vCard 2.1 cards, including quoted-printable, `CHARSET`, `BASE64` and the card an `AGENT` holds, with `VcardReader` and `VcardOptions.WriteVersion`, and view them through `IVcard21Card`
`VcardOptions.WriteNamedTypesInVersion21` writes each `TYPE` of a vCard 2.1 card with its name, as `TEL;TYPE=WORK:`

95a507a0de97a30c38d2862c5bc70d3c66b487da.subject: VcardCard.Photos, Logos and Sounds hold media of any length on every target (#682)

cb96d3954d0f80fbb65cfe39ef5f100fa8a943cb.subject: VcardContentLineReader rejects a byte order mark whatever VcardOptions.Encoding is (#694)

fba3d302cdcc9a4cf0d53149baf9b65bf21c202d.subject: VcardWriter, JcardWriter, XcardWriter and VcardContentLineReader cancel an asynchronous operation only when the caller's token is canceled (#713)

34f74b2eac494acd3127ad0f4f1d0f751e53dbbf.subject: VcardReader, JcardReader and XcardReader cancel an asynchronous read only when the caller's token is canceled (#721)

f397569629a30ec7c3e77c6ba0311b9ff24106b8.subject: StringEnum.Parse and TryParse with ignoreCase no longer throw when two member names differ only by case (#729)

notes.text: Bcp47LanguageTag's ReadOnlySpan<char> overloads and AsSpan() are now available on netstandard1.1

023c6202967adf0222ab4cb042d8d414b30a7606.subject: IcalReader and IcalWriter reject a quoted value for a parameter whose grammar has no quoted form (#675)

notes.text: `IcalReader` rejects, and `IcalWriter` refuses to write, a parameter value in double quotes where the parameter's grammar has no quoted form, such as `FMTTYPE="audio/basic"` (RFC 5545 §3.2.8)
`IcalOptions.AllowQuotedParameterValues` accepts a quoted value for a parameter whose grammar has no quoted form, reported as the new `IcalDiagnosticKind.QuotedParameterValue`.

40a6745312f976263b202d2ca54d3e892740a943.subject: A double constant with a decimal scale above 22 converts to a decimal property (#923)

141264128a1f58039a0c2c634140ebd11ecd4d6e.subject: A field mapping with another field name keeps its values when a line is read or written (#869)

notes.text: A property mapped to a field with another name now reads and writes that field's value

44feff8b4177e26c9659937f65be9434a779f989.subject: A field index mapping reads the field at that position of the record (#870)

notes.text: A property mapped by index reads the field at that position of the record, not another column
A required mapping whose field the record doesn't have, by name or by index, throws `CsvFileException` instead of giving the property its default value

57ea2b771df8d8e11d706f0bf83a17ed64d0d0ca.subject: CsvFileWriter writes nothing for a line that InconsistentFieldCountHandler handled (#874)

notes.text: `CsvFileWriter.WriteLine` writes nothing for a line that `InconsistentFieldCountHandler` handled, instead of a blank record
Without a header line, a record line that `CsvFileWriter.WriteLine` handled as inconsistent or threw for no longer adds its fields to later lines

8b71143f64eeccfe909cbc6e4070db737a01a862.subject: CsvFileWriter without a header no longer drops the values of a field the first record line doesn't have (#875)

notes.text: Without a header line, `CsvFileWriter.WriteLine` no longer drops the value of a field the first record line doesn't have; it handles the line as an inconsistent field count

69b2e1016d3d6d2cca193db4fb4da37b0d589ba1.subject: CsvFileWriter with SuppressTrailingBlankFields no longer drops values or keeps blanks when a record line's fields are in another order (#876)

notes.text: `CsvFileWriter` with `SuppressTrailingBlankFields` no longer drops values or keeps blanks when a record line's fields are in another order
`SuppressTrailingBlankFields` judges a trailing field by the text written for it: a converter writing nothing leaves it out, and a constant or generated value is written

e82f9a9c31f967387f3980feeddb82e57257dbba.subject: CsvFileReader rejects whitespace around a quoted field and a line break in an unquoted field (#880)

f6b8f498f813c269bbeaa0c85aebb8e7cffbd53c.subject: CsvFieldConvertFromString and CsvFieldValidate contexts give the field's raw value and its position in the line (#891)

notes.text: `CsvFieldConvertFromString` and `CsvFieldValidate` contexts give the field's raw value and position, and `CsvFieldConvertToString` contexts the position and name of the field written

671ac391cf411a30a811ae33c0ad5d1d2dc508fc.subject: CsvFieldConvertToString context gives the position and name of the field being written (#921)

1ec71b2067b7c25148a5c8e8251cb189196230fa.subject: Configured converters now run for string properties on read and write (#893)

notes.text: `ConvertUsing` delegates and type converters configured for a `string` property now run on read and write, instead of being skipped

0136a30810e2527eec1f2efc3c72418c403231a2.subject: File.CSV mapping now covers inherited properties and their attributes (#894)

notes.text: Mapping covers inherited properties and their attributes, so a `[CsvField]` or `[CsvFieldMapping]` on a base class applies to derived record lines and models

b197f36289e4683aee7896fb1be4c90b8ec6f6ac.subject: CsvFileReader no longer throws ArgumentException when a generated field name matches another field's name (#895)

notes.text: `CsvFileReader` no longer throws `ArgumentException` when a header or mapped field is named like a generated `Field N`; it reports an inconsistent field count or renames the generated field `Field N (2)`

4c7501fc6c00d0f2804401a936e512c130e13273.subject: CsvFileRecordLine properties throw InvalidCastException for a field value they can't return, instead of reading as the default (#896)

notes.text: A `CsvFileRecordLine` property that calls `GetPropertyValue<T>` throws `InvalidCastException` when its field holds another type's value instead of returning the default; map the property to convert it

e2d009f7079b1e40e0ccd8f439b8a233cf2ee005.subject: CsvFileWriter no longer drops a record line's fields that aren't in the header line or mapper (#897)

notes.text: `CsvFileWriter` no longer drops a record line's fields that aren't in the header line or mapper; a field not in the header line makes the line inconsistent

89f6e89a7170b7a6cba390449bdb58c1f6495ca7.subject: CsvFileReader and CsvFileWriter throw ArgumentException for a handler they would never call, instead of ignoring it (#899)

notes.text: `CsvFileReader` and `CsvFileWriter` throw `ArgumentException` for a `BadValueHandler`, `InconsistentFieldCountHandler` or `HeaderHandler` of a type they never call, instead of ignoring it

51a2403f90bf59cb8c6478618f450f05b494cfb2.subject: ToObject and ToCsvLine apply the whole mapper, not just field names (#900)

notes.text: `ToObject` and `ToCsvLine` apply the whole custom mapper, not just its field names
`ToObject` no longer falls back to the field named after the property when the mapping names a field the line doesn't have

13c723180ebf68f3504531f92e17fbade7267d9f.subject: A mapped constant of another number type is converted to the property's type instead of reading as the default (#901)

notes.text: A mapped `ConstantValue` of another number type, such as `5` on a `long` property, converts to the property's type, and one the type can't hold, such as `-1` on a `byte`, throws `CsvFileException`, instead of reading as the default

f2254a9b063b38fb6320501f8988b676b3d5f43e.subject: CsvFileWriter writes dates and floating-point values so they read back unchanged, as the same text on every target (#905)

notes.text: `CsvFileWriter` writes a `DateTime`, `DateTimeOffset`, `DateOnly` or `TimeOnly` it has no converter for with the round-trip pattern (`"o"`), keeping fractional seconds, `Kind` and offset
`CsvFileWriter` writes a `double` or `float` it has no converter for in the fewest digits that read back as the same value, as the same text on every target
A `DateTime` field with a UTC designator (`Z` or `GMT`) reads as UTC, with `DateTimeKind.Utc`, instead of being converted to the machine's local time
On `net10.0`, a `DateOnly` field in the round-trip pattern (`yyyy-MM-dd`) reads as that Gregorian date in every culture

5cd8f5bd0e47e52a0e43e53f5ad053ca1c033161.subject: CsvFileReader calls the header handler with the file's header line, whatever the header handling (#908)

notes.text: A header handler is called whatever the header handling, with the file's header line; with `CsvFileHeaderHandling.Use` it was ignored, and with `Ignore` passed null
A header handler must return as many field names as each record is expected to have, none of them null, or `ReadLine` throws `InvalidOperationException`
With `CsvFileHeaderHandling.Ignore` and a header handler, a header line that repeats a field name makes `ReadLine` throw `CsvFileException`

262bf0be2679f53c34d3cb4347971aedcbf5b17a.subject: A builder mapping of a property with [CsvField] now reads and writes the field that attribute names (#909)

notes.text: A `Map().Property()` mapping of a property with `[CsvField]` uses the field that attribute names for reading, writing and its key, as a declarative mapping does

c1cb5c393e5b1115f02efddc9c8a96fa25ee5072.subject: CsvFileWriter no longer writes a header or record line with no fields as an empty line (#911)

notes.text: `CsvFileWriter.WriteLine` no longer writes a header or record line with no fields as an empty line; it throws `CsvFileException`, or calls `InconsistentFieldCountHandler` for a record line

43c26a3598c5ced0d96c0f50bd417b30c1a06023.subject: CsvFileWriter rejects options whose output can't be read back (#912)

notes.text: `CsvFileWriter` throws `ArgumentException` for options whose output can't be read back: an empty or `null` `TerminatorLineBreak`, a `FieldDelimiterCharacter` that is a quote or starts the terminator, a terminator starting with a quote, or an undefined `QuoteHandling`
On .NET Standard, `CsvFileWriter.WriteLine` throws `InvalidOperationException`, and writes nothing, when the options have been changed to such values

92108b4b9dd2d3662309dfe2b401834a67c91d27.subject: CsvFileReader and CsvFileWriter reject characters outside RFC 4180 TEXTDATA by default (#914)

notes.text: `CsvFileReader` reports a field holding a control character, such as TAB, or a character outside its encoding as a bad value, and `CsvFileWriter` throws `CsvFileException` for one, as RFC 4180 `TEXTDATA` requires
`CsvFileWriter.WriteLine` throws `InvalidOperationException` when the field delimiter or terminator holds a character its encoding can't write, or `EmbeddedLineBreak` one that isn't printable in it

b832341555cb08dd074c79a4d81c0c6f9ceadd0a.subject: CsvFileWriter writes a field mapped by index at its index, so the same mapper reads the file back (#917)

notes.text: `CsvFileWriter` writes a field mapped by index at its index, so the same mapper reads the file back
`CsvFileWriter` puts a header line's index-mapped fields at their indexes, its other mapped fields in the gaps and unmapped ones last, and a record line's unmapped fields in the gaps
Without a header line, a field mapped by name takes the first position no other mapping takes, so one mapped after a field index fills the gap below that index
`CsvFileWriter` throws `CsvFileException` for a header line with no field for a required mapping by name, which a reader with the same mapper couldn't read

6138c8face0f7cb02911c33f3fa9d60903bf4e70.subject: CsvFileReader gives each property mapped to a shared field the field's value, whatever its type (#919)

notes.text: Properties of different types mapped to the same field each read the field's value, instead of 0 and null
A mapping of a field the file doesn't have no longer reads the value another mapping's constant or generator adds for it: an optional one is skipped, a required one throws `CsvFileException`

fc973f462bc3b517ab71ec287dc6e2ff149e2062.subject: CsvFileReader reads a header line that repeats a field name, as RFC 4180 allows (#920)

notes.text: `CsvFileReader` reads a header line that repeats a field name, as RFC 4180 allows, when the mapper gives each field of that name a name of its own
`UseFieldName` on a field mapping, and `CsvFieldMappingAttribute.UseFieldName`, give a field the name it is known by once read; `CsvFileWriter` writes it under its name in the file

f0e6e2b2fb3f89e25988a7d43bc340ed5e2f712f.subject: CsvFileOptions and CsvFieldContext compare by value on .NET Standard, as on net10.0 (#913)

notes.text: On .NET Standard, `CsvFileOptions` and `CsvFieldContext<TModel>` compare by value and print their properties from `ToString`, as on .NET 10

c2666811ab96dfad75dd30af12e1cb465b183e14.subject: CsvFileWriter writes a mapped property's own value when its key is the name of another property with [CsvField] (#926)

notes.text: `CsvFileWriter` writes a mapped property's own value when its field name or `[CsvField]` name is another property's `[CsvField]` key, instead of that property's value

4e698e3520ef41da6074fd511a1d7778421a3831.subject: CsvFileWriter writes a mapped property's own value when its field name is another property's key (#929)

notes.text: A property of a line read through a mapping reads as not set when the record has no field for it, instead of the value of another field named like its `[CsvField]` key

d7e4ff670213f7d81c1d5ccfb9942ef66100d3b7.subject: CsvFileReader reports a byte its encoding can't decode as a bad value (#928)

notes.text: `CsvFileReader` reports a field holding a lone surrogate, or bytes that aren't valid in the file's encoding, as a bad value, instead of reading U+FFFD or `?`
`CsvFileReader` reads a file in `CsvFileOptions.Encoding` even when it starts with the byte order mark of another encoding
`CsvFileWriter` throws `CsvFileException`, not `EncoderFallbackException`, for a value that holds a lone surrogate
